metadata.title: Testing Graph Properties with the Container Method

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-far from a graph property
nodes.statement: A simple undirected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is $\epsilon$-far from a graph property $\Pi$ if at least $\epsilon n^2$ edges must be added or removed from $G$ to obtain a graph that has property $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Canonical $\epsilon$-tester
nodes.statement: A bounded-error randomized algorithm that samples a set $S$ of $s$ vertices of an unknown graph $G$, examines the induced subgraph $G[S]$, and based only on this local view distinguishes between $G$ having property $\Pi$ and $G$ being $\epsilon$-far from $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Sample complexity $\mathcal{S}_\Pi(n,\epsilon)$
nodes.statement: The sample complexity of property $\Pi$, denoted $\mathcal{S}_\Pi(n,\epsilon)$, is the minimum value $s$ for which there is a canonical $\epsilon$-tester for $\Pi$ with sample cost $s$.

nodes.name: $\rho$-Clique property
nodes.statement: The set of all graphs on $n$ vertices that contain a clique on $\rho n$ vertices.

nodes.name: $\rho$-IndepSet property
nodes.statement: The set of all graphs on $n$ vertices that contain an independent set on $\rho n$ vertices (the complement of the $\rho$-Clique property).

nodes.name: $k$-Colorable property
nodes.statement: The set of all graphs on $n$ vertices that are $k$-colorable. The case $k=2$ corresponds to bipartiteness.

nodes.name: Fingerprint and Container of an independent set
nodes.statement: Given a graph $G$ and independent set $I$, the $t$-th fingerprint $F_t(I)$ and $t$-th container $C_t(I)$ are produced by the greedy procedure of Algorithm 1, with the convention $C_t = F_t = I$ for $t > |I|$.

nodes.name: Testing the $\rho$-Clique property
nodes.statement: Determine $\mathcal{S}_{\rho\textsc{-Clique}}(n,\epsilon)$: the minimum sample size $s$ such that a canonical tester can distinguish graphs containing a $\rho n$-clique from graphs $\epsilon$-far from the $\rho$-Clique property.

nodes.name: Testing $k$-Colorability
nodes.statement: Determine $\mathcal{S}_{k\textsc{-Colorable}}(n,\epsilon)$: the minimum sample size $s$ such that a canonical tester can distinguish $k$-colorable graphs from those $\epsilon$-far from $k$-colorable.

nodes.name: Densest $k$-Subgraph (D$k$S) decision problem
nodes.statement: Distinguish graphs that contain a $k$-clique from graphs whose $k$-subgraphs all contain at most $(1-\delta)\binom{k}{2}$ edges.

nodes.name: Planted $k$-Clique Detection
nodes.statement: Distinguish random graphs with edge probability $(1-\delta)$ from random graphs with edge probability $(1-\delta)$ containing a planted $k$-clique.

nodes.name: Fingerprint & Container Generator
nodes.statement: Greedy procedure (variant of Kleitman-Winston) that, given graph $G$ and independent set $I$, produces sequences of fingerprints $F_1,\dots,F_{|I|}$ and containers $C_1,\dots,C_{|I|}$ by repeatedly selecting the highest-degree remaining vertex of $I$ and pruning higher-degree vertices and neighbours.

nodes.name: Canonical tester for $\rho$-IndepSet
nodes.statement: Sample $s = c \cdot \frac{\rho^3}{\epsilon^2} \ln^3(1/\epsilon)$ vertices uniformly without replacement and accept iff the induced subgraph $G[S]$ contains an independent set of size $\rho s$.
output: Accept if $G[S]$ contains a $\rho s$-independent set; reject otherwise

nodes.name: Canonical tester for $k$-Colorable
nodes.statement: Sample $s = c \cdot \frac{k}{\epsilon} \ln^2(1/\epsilon)$ vertices uniformly without replacement and accept iff the induced subgraph $G[S]$ is $k$-colorable.

nodes.name: Sample complexity of $\rho$-Clique testing (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: The sample complexity of the $\rho$-Clique property is $\mathcal{S}_{\rho\textsc{-Clique}}(n,\epsilon) = \tilde{O}\!\left(\frac{\rho^3}{\epsilon^2}\right)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1' (Alternative formulation, Densest $k$-Subgraph)
nodes.statement: For every $n$, $k = k(n) < n$, and $\delta = \delta(n) > 0$, there is a bounded-error randomized algorithm that distinguishes graphs containing a $k$-clique from graphs whose $k$-subgraphs all contain at most $(1-\delta)\binom{k}{2}$ edges by inspecting an induced subgraph on $|S| = O\!\left(\frac{n}{\delta^2 k}\ln^3\!\left(\frac{n}{\delta^2 k}\right)\right)$ random vertices.
conclusions: Sample size $|S| = O\!\left(\frac{n}{\delta^2 k}\ln^3\!\left(\frac{n}{\delta^2 k}\right)\right)$ suffices for the stated distinguishing task

nodes.name: Sample complexity of $k$-Colorable testing (Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: The $k$-Colorable property has sample complexity $\mathcal{S}_{k\textsc{-Colorable}}(n,\epsilon) = \tilde{O}\!\left(\frac{k}{\epsilon}\right)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (precise) for $\rho$-IndepSet
nodes.statement: The sample complexity of the $\rho$-IndepSet property is $\mathcal{S}_{\rho\textsc{-IndepSet}}(n,\epsilon) = O\!\left(\frac{\rho^3}{\epsilon^2}\ln^3(1/\epsilon)\right)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (precise) for $k$-Colorable
nodes.statement: The sample complexity of the $k$-Colorable property is $\mathcal{S}_{k\textsc{-Colorable}}(n,\epsilon) = O\!\left(\frac{k}{\epsilon}\ln^2(1/\epsilon)\right)$.

nodes.name: Graph Container Lemma I
nodes.statement: For any graph $G$ on $n$ vertices that is $\epsilon$-far from $\rho$-IndepSet, there exist a fingerprint family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^V$ and container function $\mathcal{C}: \mathcal{F} \to 2^V$ such that every large independent set $I$ has some $F \in \mathcal{F}$ with $F \subseteq I \subseteq \mathcal{C}(F)$, with $|F| \le \frac{8\rho^2 \ln(2\rho/\epsilon)}{\epsilon}$ and $|\mathcal{C}(F)| \le (\rho - |F|\cdot \frac{\epsilon}{8\rho \ln(2\rho/\epsilon)}) n$.

nodes.name: Graph Container Lemma II
nodes.statement: If $G$ is $\epsilon$-far from $k$-colorable, then there exist a fingerprint family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq (2^V)^k$ and container function $\mathcal{C}: \mathcal{F} \to 2^V$ such that every $k$-colorable $U \subseteq V$ with $|U| \geq 4k/\epsilon$ has some $F = (T_1,\ldots,T_k)$ with $\bigcup_i T_i \subseteq U \subseteq \mathcal{C}(F)$, $|T_i| \le 4/\epsilon$, and $|\mathcal{C}(F)| \le (1 - \frac{\epsilon}{4\ln(1/\epsilon)}\max_i |T_i|) n$.

nodes.name: Container Shrinking Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be $\epsilon$-far from $\rho$-IndepSet, $I$ an independent set in $G$, and $t < |I|$ with $|C_t| \ge \rho n$. For any $\alpha > 0$, if $C \subseteq C_{t+1}$ has $|C| = (\rho - \alpha)n$ and $G[C]$ has at most $\frac{\epsilon}{4} n^2$ edges, then $|C_{t+1}\setminus C| \le (1 - \frac{\epsilon}{4\rho\alpha})|C_t \setminus C|$.

nodes.name: Graph Container Lemma I (alternative formulation)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be $\epsilon$-far from $\rho$-IndepSet. For any independent set $I$ there exists $t \le \frac{8\rho^2}{\epsilon}\ln(2\rho/\epsilon)$ such that $|C_t| \le (\rho - t \cdot \frac{\epsilon}{8\rho\ln(2\rho/\epsilon)}) n$ and $G[C_t]$ contains at most $\epsilon n^2/4$ edges.

nodes.name: Graph Container Lemma II (alternative formulation)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be $\epsilon$-far from $k$-colorable, $I_1,\dots,I_k$ independent sets in $G$. There exists $t \le 4/\epsilon$ with $|\bigcup_{i=1}^k C_t(I_i)| \le (1 - t\cdot \frac{\epsilon}{4\ln(1/\epsilon)}) n$.

nodes.name: Chernoff's Bound for hypergeometric distribution
nodes.statement: Let $X \sim H(N,K,m)$ be hypergeometric. For any $\vartheta \geq \E[X]$, $\Pr[X \ge \vartheta] \le \exp\!\left(-\frac{(\vartheta - \E[X])^2}{\vartheta + \E[X]}\right)$.

nodes.name: Container closure property
nodes.statement: For any graph $G$, independent set $I$, and index $t$: $C_t(F_t(I)) = C_t(I)$.

nodes.name: Container maximum-degree bound
nodes.statement: For any graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, independent set $I$, and $t \ge 1$, the $t$-th container of $I$ satisfies $\Delta(G[C_t]) \le n/t$.

nodes.name: Container chain inclusion
nodes.statement: $F_1 \subseteq F_2 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq F_{|I|} = I \subseteq C_{|I|} \subseteq \cdots \subseteq C_2 \subseteq C_1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Container closure property
nodes.statement: If $t > |I|$, $F_t(I) = I = C_t(I)$ trivially. Otherwise, the greedy algorithm selects the same first $t$ vertices and produces the same container when given $F_t(I)$ as when given $I$.

nodes.name: Proof of Container maximum-degree bound
nodes.statement: By averaging on the telescoping sum $\sum_i |C_{i-1}\setminus C_i| \le n$, some round $j \le t$ removes at most $n/t$ vertices, forcing the chosen $v_j$ and all surviving vertices in $C_j \supseteq C_t$ to have degree $\le n/t$ in their induced subgraph.

nodes.name: Proof of Container Shrinking Lemma
nodes.statement: Lower-bound $|C_t \setminus C_{t+1}|$ by case analysis on whether $C$ contains a high-degree vertex; otherwise show $G[C_t \setminus C]$ is dense via a random-subset argument using $\epsilon$-farness.

nodes.name: Proof of Graph Container Lemma I (alternative)
nodes.statement: Take $C$ as the first container with $\le \epsilon n^2/4$ edges and $|C| = (\rho - \alpha)n$. Apply the Container Shrinking Lemma iteratively to bound $t^*$, then bound the remaining iterations to obtain the index bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Graph Container Lemma I
nodes.statement: Define $\mathcal{F}$ as the fingerprints $F_{t_I}(I)$ over large independent sets $I$ and $\mathcal{C}(F) = C_{|F|}(F)$; cardinality bounds and the covering property follow from the alternative formulation and container closure.

nodes.name: Proof of Graph Container Lemma II (alternative)
nodes.statement: Argue by contradiction: if every container union were too large, build a $k$-partition by allocating the $A_t$ layers and bound the resulting monochromatic edges by $< \epsilon n^2$, contradicting $\epsilon$-farness from $k$-colorable.

nodes.name: Proof of Graph Container Lemma II
nodes.statement: Define $\mathcal{F}$ from arbitrary $k$-partitions of $k$-colorable $U$ and $\mathcal{C}(F) = \bigcup_i C_{\max_j |T_j|}(T_i)$; combine the alternative formulation with container closure to obtain the bounds.

nodes.name: Proof of Chernoff's Bound for hypergeometric
nodes.statement: Apply the standard multiplicative Chernoff inequality with $\delta = (\vartheta - \E[X])/\E[X]$ and simplify; the multiplicative bound also applies to hypergeometric variables.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (precise) for $\rho$-IndepSet
nodes.statement: Sample $s = c \rho^3 \epsilon^{-2} \ln^3(1/\epsilon)$ vertices. Completeness via hypergeometric median. Soundness: union-bound over $\mathcal{F}$ from Lemma I, applying the Chernoff bound to the conditional containment probability.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (precise) for $k$-Colorable
nodes.statement: Sample $s = c k\epsilon^{-1} \ln^2(1/\epsilon)$ vertices. Completeness is immediate. Soundness: union-bound over fingerprint sequences from Lemma II, bounding the conditional containment probability by $(1 - \frac{\epsilon}{4\ln(1/\epsilon)}\cdot \frac{t}{k})^{s-t}$.

nodes.name: Tight version of Lemma I covering all $I$
nodes.statement: Lemma I can be extended to cover any independent set (not only those with $|I| \geq \frac{8\rho^2}{\epsilon}\ln(2\rho/\epsilon)$) by a slight variation in the fingerprint definition; this strengthening is unnecessary for Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Completeness probability and error reduction
nodes.statement: The tester's $1/2$ completeness can be boosted to $2/3$ via standard error reduction at a $\ln(1/\gamma)$ multiplicative cost, or directly by relaxing the inner check to the $(\rho-\tau)$-IndepSet property.

nodes.name: Optimality of $\tilde{O}(k/\epsilon)$ bound
nodes.statement: Determine whether the bound $\mathcal{S}_{k\textsc{-Colorable}}(n,\epsilon) = \tilde{O}(k/\epsilon)$ in Theorem 2 is optimal; the best known lower bound in the polychromatic regime is $\tilde{\Omega}(1/\epsilon)$, leaving a quadratic gap.

nodes.name: Container method for broader testing problems
nodes.statement: Identify the largest class of graph (and hypergraph) properties for which the (hyper)graph container method yields tight property-testing bounds, beyond the 0--1 graph partition properties studied in subsequent work.

nodes.name: Bogdanov-Li bipartiteness query conjecture
nodes.statement: It is possible to $\frac{1}{n}$-test 2-colorability (bipartiteness) with $o(n^2)$ queries.

nodes.name: Goldreich-Goldwasser-Ron clique upper bound
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{S}_{\rho\textsc{-Clique}}(n,\epsilon) = \tilde{O}(\rho/\epsilon^4)$.

nodes.name: Feige-Langberg-Schechtman clique bounds
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{S}_{\rho\textsc{-Clique}}(n,\epsilon) = \tilde{O}(\rho^4/\epsilon^3)$ and $\mathcal{S}_{\rho\textsc{-Clique}}(n,\epsilon) = \tilde{\Omega}(\rho^3/\epsilon^2)$.

nodes.name: Alon-Krivelevich $k$-colorability bound
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{S}_{k\textsc{-Colorable}}(n,\epsilon) = \tilde{O}(k/\epsilon^2)$ for all $k \ge 3$.

nodes.name: Sohler $k$-colorability bound
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{S}_{k\textsc{-Colorable}}(n,\epsilon) = \tilde{O}(k^6/\epsilon)$; in particular for constant $k$, $\tilde{\Theta}(1/\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Setup: relate $|C_{t+1}\setminus C|$ to $|C_t\setminus C|$
nodes.statement: Use $C \subseteq C_{t+1} \subseteq C_t$ to obtain $|C_{t+1}\setminus C| = |C_t\setminus C| - |C_t\setminus C_{t+1}|$ and aim to lower-bound $|C_t\setminus C_{t+1}|$.

nodes.name: Case 1: high-degree vertex in $C$
nodes.statement: If some $v \in C$ has degree $\ge \frac{\epsilon}{4\rho\alpha}|C_t\setminus C|$ in $G[C_t]$, then the greedy choice $v_{t+1}$ has degree at least as large, so at least this many vertices are removed.

nodes.name: Case 2: claim $G[C_t\setminus C]$ is dense
nodes.statement: If all $v \in C$ have low degree in $G[C_t]$, claim $G[C_t\setminus C]$ has $\ge \frac{\epsilon}{4\rho\alpha}|C_t\setminus C|^2$ edges, which forces $\frac{\epsilon}{4\rho\alpha}|C_t\setminus C|$ removals.

nodes.name: Random-subset argument for density
nodes.statement: Pick a uniform random $R \subseteq C_t\setminus C$ of size $\alpha n$; using $\epsilon$-farness, $G[R\cup C]$ has $\ge \epsilon n^2$ edges, while $G[C]$ contributes $\le \epsilon n^2/4$ and $C\textrm{-to-}C_t\setminus C$ edges contribute at most $\frac{\epsilon}{4} n^2$ in expectation.

nodes.name: Conclude expected density of $G[R]$
nodes.statement: Combine the bounds: $\E[\textrm{edges in }G[R]] \ge \frac{\epsilon}{2}n^2 \ge \frac{\epsilon}{\alpha^2}\binom{|R|}{2}$, so $G[C_t\setminus C]$ has density $\ge \epsilon/\alpha^2$ and the desired edge bound follows.

nodes.name: Choose first sparse container $C$
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be the first container with $\le \epsilon n^2/4$ edges; existence follows since $C_{|I|+1} = I$ has no edges. Write $|C| = (\rho - \alpha) n$ with $\frac{\epsilon}{2\rho} \le \alpha \le \rho$.

nodes.name: Iterate Container Shrinking up to $t^*$
nodes.statement: Let $t^*$ be the largest index with $|C_{t^*}| \ge \rho n$. Apply the Container Shrinking Lemma for $t = 0,\dots,t^*-1$ to get $|C_{t^*}\setminus C| \le (1 - \frac{\epsilon}{4\rho\alpha})^{t^*} n$; conclude $t^* \le \frac{4\rho\alpha}{\epsilon}\ln(2\rho/\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Bound iterations beyond $t^*$
nodes.statement: For $t > t^*$, while $G[C_t]$ has $> \epsilon n^2/4$ edges, at least $\epsilon n/(4\rho)$ vertices are removed per round; hence at most $4\rho\alpha/\epsilon$ such rounds occur before $C_t$ becomes $C$.

nodes.name: Combine and rearrange
nodes.statement: Total iterations are $\le \frac{8\rho\alpha}{\epsilon}\ln(2\rho/\epsilon)$; rearranging for $\alpha$ recovers the conclusion of the lemma.

nodes.name: Setup contradiction
nodes.statement: Assume that for all $t \le 4/\epsilon$, $|\bigcup_i C_t(I_i)| > (1 - t\cdot \frac{\epsilon}{4\ln(1/\epsilon)}) n$, and aim to construct a $k$-partition violating $\epsilon$-farness from $k$-colorable.

nodes.name: Initialize partition from final containers
nodes.statement: Set $V_i = C_{4/\epsilon}(I_i)$ for each $i$, prune duplicates so $V_1,\dots,V_k$ partition $\bigcup_i C_{4/\epsilon}(I_i)$. By Proposition 2.2 each vertex has degree $\le \epsilon n/4$ in its set, contributing $\le \epsilon n^2/4$ edges total.

nodes.name: Define removal layers $A_t$
nodes.statement: Let $A_t = \{v \in V : v \in \bigcup_i C_{t-1}(I_i),\ v \notin \bigcup_i C_t(I_i)\}$ for $t = 1,\dots,4/\epsilon$; the $A_t$'s partition $V \setminus \bigcup_i C_{4/\epsilon}(I_i)$.

nodes.name: Allocate remaining vertices and bound new edges
nodes.statement: For each $v \in A_t$, add $v$ to some $V_i$ with $v \in C_{t-1}(I_i)$. Processing in reverse order ensures $V_i \subseteq C_{t-1}(I_i)$ at the time of addition; by Proposition 2.2, $v$ contributes $\le n/(t-1)$ new edges (or $n$ for $t=1$).

nodes.name: Bound total edges via harmonic sum
nodes.statement: Total edges $\le \frac{\epsilon n^2}{4} + |A_1| n + \sum_{t=2}^{4/\epsilon} |A_t| \frac{n}{t-1}$. Using $\sum_{\ell\le t}|A_\ell| \le \frac{t\epsilon n}{4\ln(1/\epsilon)}$ and the harmonic bound $H(m)\le \ln m + 1$, conclude total $< \epsilon n^2$, contradicting $\epsilon$-farness.

nodes.name: Completeness via hypergeometric median
nodes.statement: If $G$ contains a $\rho n$ independent set, then $|S \cap I| \ge \rho s$ with probability $\ge 1/2$ since the hypergeometric distribution's median is $\ge \rho s$.

nodes.name: Cover bad event by fingerprint family
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma I: if $G[S]$ contains an independent set of size $\rho s > \frac{8\rho^2}{\epsilon}\ln(2\rho/\epsilon)$, some $F \in \mathcal{F}$ satisfies $F \subseteq S$ and $|S \cap \mathcal{C}(F)| \ge \rho s$.

nodes.name: Bound $\Pr[F \subseteq S]$
nodes.statement: Standard counting gives $\Pr[F \subseteq S] \le \binom{n-|F|}{s-|F|}/\binom{n}{s} = \binom{s}{|F|}/\binom{n}{|F|}$.

nodes.name: Apply Chernoff to conditional containment
nodes.statement: With $t = |F|$, bound $\E[X] < \rho s - t - \frac{t\epsilon s}{16\rho\ln(2\rho/\epsilon)}$ and apply Lemma 4 to obtain $\Pr[X \ge \rho s - t] \le \exp(-\frac{t^2\epsilon^2 s}{512\rho^3\ln^2(2\rho/\epsilon)})$.

nodes.name: Union bound over fingerprints
nodes.statement: Sum over $t \le \frac{8\rho^2 \ln(2\rho/\epsilon)}{\epsilon}$ and over $F$ of size $t$ using $\binom{s}{t} \le s^t$; the total is $< 1/3$ for $s = c\rho^3 \epsilon^{-2}\ln^3(1/\epsilon)$ with large enough $c$.

nodes.name: Completeness
nodes.statement: If $G$ is $k$-colorable then $G[S]$ is $k$-colorable, so the tester always accepts.

nodes.name: Cover bad event using Lemma II
nodes.statement: By Lemma II, $G[S]$ being $k$-colorable forces some $F = (T_1,\dots,T_k) \in \mathcal{F}$ with $\bigcup_i T_i \subseteq S \subseteq \mathcal{C}(F)$.

nodes.name: Bound $\Pr[\bigcup_i T_i \subseteq S]$ and $\Pr[S \subseteq \mathcal{C}(F) \mid \cdot]$
nodes.statement: With $t = |\bigcup_i T_i|$: $\Pr[\bigcup_i T_i \subseteq S] \le \binom{s}{t}/\binom{n}{t}$; conditional containment $\le (1 - \frac{\epsilon}{4\ln(1/\epsilon)}\max_i |T_i|)^{s-t}$ from Lemma II.

nodes.name: Sum over fingerprint sequences
nodes.statement: There are $\le \binom{n}{t}\cdot k^t$ choices of $F$ with $|\bigcup_i T_i| = t$; using $\max_i |T_i| \ge t/k$, total bound becomes $\sum_t k^t \binom{s}{t}(1 - \frac{\epsilon t}{4k\ln(1/\epsilon)})^{s-t}$.

nodes.name: Final exponent estimate
nodes.statement: Use $s > 2t$, $\binom{s}{t} \le s^t$ and $\ln(k/\epsilon)\le 2\ln(1/\epsilon)$ to bound the sum by $\sum_t \exp(t\ln(sk) - \frac{\epsilon t s}{8k\ln(1/\epsilon)}) < 1/3$ for $s = ck\epsilon^{-1}\ln^2(1/\epsilon)$ with large enough $c$.

nodes.name: Initialize $F_0$ and $C_0$
nodes.statement: Set $F_0 \gets \emptyset$ and $C_0 \gets V$.

nodes.name: Greedy selection loop over $t = 1,\dots,|I|$
nodes.statement: For each $t$: choose $v_t$ as the vertex in $I \setminus F_{t-1}$ with the largest degree in $G[C_{t-1}]$ (ties broken by a fixed vertex ordering); update $F_t \gets F_{t-1}\cup\{v_t\}$; remove from $C_{t-1}$ all neighbours of $v_t$ and all vertices with strictly higher degree than $v_t$ in $G[C_{t-1}]$ to obtain $C_t$.

nodes.name: Return fingerprint and container sequences
nodes.statement: Return $F_1,\ldots,F_{|I|}$ and $C_1,\ldots,C_{|I|}$.

nodes.name: Sample vertex set $S$
nodes.statement: Draw $s = c\cdot \frac{\rho^3}{\epsilon^2}\ln^3(1/\epsilon)$ vertices uniformly without replacement from $V$.

nodes.name: Test induced subgraph for large independent set
nodes.statement: Accept iff $G[S]$ contains an independent set of size $\rho s$.

nodes.name: Sample vertex set $S$
nodes.statement: Draw $s = c\cdot \frac{k}{\epsilon}\ln^2(1/\epsilon)$ vertices uniformly without replacement from $V$.

nodes.name: Test induced subgraph for $k$-colorability
nodes.statement: Accept iff $G[S]$ is $k$-colorable.
